quotes.text: But here's the catch. The rules it enforces depend heavily on the structure you've set up. If information architecture is sloppy, Perview enforces chaos. If ia is solid, perview enforces order.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Core thesis of the episode: Purview amplifies whatever information architecture it finds.

quotes.text: Copilot depends on accurate index content. If your IA is clean, Copilot actually serves up useful answers because it's grounded in the right data. But with poor IA, the risk spikes.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: Map your content, standardize names and metadata, and always pilot before scaling. Do those three things, and Purview shifts from being a problem generator to a compliance ally that actually works for you instead of against you.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concise, actionable three-step recommendation that sums up the episode.

takeaways: Microsoft Purview enforces retention and classification rules exactly as configured, so weak information architecture turns it into a blunt instrument.
Broad retention policies lock files, preserve junk and inflate storage, and some label settings are hard or impossible to roll back, so pilot in a small scope first.
Mapping content, enforcing naming and a few required metadata fields, cleaning up before lockdown and piloting make both Purview and Copilot more precise.
hook: One wrong Purview retention rule can lock files, bloat storage and flood your helpdesk with tickets. This episode is for information architects and Microsoft 365 admins who need compliance without chaos. Learn the IA guardrails and pilot plan that make Purview and Copilot work for you.
